'''Ronald Jordan "R. J." Hunter''' (born October 24, 1993) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for the [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|Georgia State Panthers]]. He is the son of Georgia State coach [[Ron Hunter]].<ref>{{cite web|title=22 R.J. Hunter|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205436545|work=[[Georgia State Panthers]]|publisher=[[Georgia State University]]|accessdate=May 23, 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Born on Oct. 24, 1993 in Oxford, Ohio to parents, [[Ron Hunter]] and Amy Hunter. His godfather is [[Ron Harper]], who played with R. J.'s dad at [[Miami University|Miami (Ohio)]] before going on to win five titles over the course of his 15-year NBA career. <ref name=GSU Player Bio>{{cite news|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=53530&SPID=5655&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=205436545&Q_SEASON=2014 |title=Player Bio: R. J. Hunter – Georgia State University Official Athletic Website |publisher=''[[Georgia State Panthers]]'' |accessdate=May 28, 2015}}</ref> R. J. is the youngest of his parents' two children. He and his older sister, Jasmine Hunter, are very close. <ref name=Ready for the NBA>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/features/chris_dortch/02/26/draft-profile-on-georgia-states-r-j-hunter/ |title=Georgia State's Hunter could be ready for jump to NBA – NBA.com |publisher=''[[NBA]]'' |date=February 26, 2015 |accessdate=May 28, 2015}}</ref>

==Collegiate career==
R. J. Hunter played three seasons for [[Georgia State University]] under his father and head coach, [[Ron Hunter]]. After his junior season, R. J. declared he would enter the [[2015 NBA Draft]].

===Freshman season===
Hunter reported a double-double with 14 points and 10 rebounds in his collegiate debut against No. 8 [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]]. He also scored 20 or more points 12 times during his freshman season, leading [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|GSU]] in scoring 15 times. Earned Kyle Macy Freshman All-America honors, [[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] Rookie-of-the-Year, All-CAA First-Team and CAA All-Rookie Team after becoming the most prolific freshman scorer in [[Georgia State University]] history. Hunter finished the year with a school-record 527 points (17 PPG avg.) and was one of just three freshmen in the country to average at least 17.0 points and 5.0 rebounds per game. <ref name=GSU Player Bio>{{cite news|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=53530&SPID=5655&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=205436545&Q_SEASON=2014 |title=Player Bio: R. J. Hunter – Georgia State University Official Athletic Website |publisher=''[[Georgia State Panthers]]'' |accessdate=May 28, 2015}}</ref>

===Sophomore season===
Hunter's trend of record setting continued into the rest of his career at [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|GSU]]. Overall, he averaged 18.4 PPG, scoring 604 for the season and became the first Panther to make 100 3-pointers in a single season. That 3-pointer count was No. 16 in the [[NCAA]]. Hunter was excellent from the free-throw line, setting the school record single-season average by hitting 88.2 percent (No. 1 percentage in the Sun Belt and No. 17 in the NCAA that season). As a part of that effort, he also set a school-record 38-straight free-throws made. On defense, Hunter finished second in the Sun Belt and 49th in the NCAA with his 63 steals.

Many know R. J. from seeing highlights of his clutch buzzer-beater in the second round of the 2015 NCAA tournament, but hitting a shot like that was nothing new for Hunter. In his sophomore year, Hunter scored a career-high 41 points against [[UTSA Roadrunners men's basketball|USTA]], making a school single-game-record 12 3-pointers. The 12 3-pointers were also the most in the country during the year and set a new [[Sun Belt Conference]] record. In another game that year, he hit the game-winning shot with 11.1 seconds to play against Arkansas State. Another clutch shot came in a game in which Hunter scored 31 points including a huge 3-pointer with seven seconds left at UT Arlington to send the game to overtime. <ref name=GSU Player Bio>{{cite news|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=53530&SPID=5655&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=205436545&Q_SEASON=2014 |title=Player Bio: R. J. Hunter – Georgia State University Official Athletic Website |publisher=''[[Georgia State Panthers]]'' |accessdate=May 28, 2015}}</ref> Hunter was named [[Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Sun Belt Conference Basketball Player of the Year]] as well as the Sun Belt Conference Male Athlete of the Year. <ref name=SUNBELT>{{cite news|url=http://sunbeltsports.org/news/2014/3/11/MBB_0311141240.aspx |title=Georgia State's Father-Son Duo Headlines Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Honorees|first=|last= |publisher=''[[Sun Belt Conference]]'' |date=March 11, 2014 |accessdate=March 11, 2014}}</ref>

===Junior season===
In his final season at [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|GSU]], R. J. Hunter averaged a career-high 19.7 points, scoring a school-record season total of 688 points (a school-record he broke each season). He also averaged 4.7 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game. In addition, he made 202 free-throws (No. 7 in the NCAA that year), second-most in school history, while swiping 75 steals, third-most in a single-season in program history. The most noteworthy record he set was total-career-points. Midway through just his third season, Hunter overtook [[Rodney Hamilton]]’s record of 1,515 points with a basket in front of a GSU home crowd against UL Lafayette on Jan. 24, 2015. R. J. finished the year with a career-total of 1,819 points.

The Panthers finished the 2014–15 season as the [[Sun Belt Conference]] regular season and tournament champions. With their Sun Belt Tournament championship win over Georgia Southern, the Panthers received a bid to the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. In the round of 64, No. 14-seed Georgia State trailed the No. 3-seed [[2014–15 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]] by 12 points with just 2:53 to play. R. J. Hunter took over and scored 12 of the Panthers' final 13 points, including a 35-foot 3-pointer with 2.6 seconds remaining to secure their electrifying come-from-behind win. The moment was selected as No. 2 in the NCAA’s top 10 moments of the tournament and was included in ‘One Shining Moment’ following the championship game. <ref name=GSU Player Bio>{{cite news|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=53530&SPID=5655&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=205436545&Q_SEASON=2014 |title=Player Bio: R. J. Hunter – Georgia State University Official Athletic Website |publisher=''[[Georgia State Panthers]]'' |accessdate=May 28, 2015}}</ref> <ref name=dagger>{{cite web|last1=Cooper|first1=Sam|title=Dramatic R. J. Hunter 3-pointer gives Georgia State upset over Baylor (Video)|url=http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaab-the-dagger/dramatic-r-j--hunter-3-pointer-gives-georgia-state-upset-over-baylor--video-201128471.html|website=''Yahoo Sports''|accessdate=19 March 2015}}</ref> 

Hunter was again named both [[Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Sun Belt Conference Basketball Player of the Year]] and the Sun Belt Conference Male Athlete of the Year. <ref name=SUNBELT>{{cite news|url=http://sunbeltsports.org/news/2014/3/11/MBB_0311141240.aspx |title=Georgia State's Father-Son Duo Headlines Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Honorees|first=|last= |publisher=''[[Sun Belt Conference]]'' |date=March 11, 2014 |accessdate=March 11, 2014}}</ref>

====College records====
* All-time Georgia State University leader in points (1,819)
* All-time Georgia State University leader in free-throws made (448); in free-throw percentage (.853); in consecutive free-throws made (38)
* All-time Georgia State University leader in 3-pointers made (253)
* Single-season Georgia State University leader in points (688, 2014–15)
* Single-season Georgia State University leader in 3-pointers made (100, 2013–14)
* Single-game [[Sun Belt Conference]] leader in 3-pointers made (12)
* Single-game [[Sun Belt Conference]] leader in free-throw percentage (1.000 16-16, 2015)

==Professional career==
R. J. has declared for the [[2015 NBA Draft]].
